The three given vertices are (5,3), (6,8), and (7,4). In a parallelogram, the diagonals bisect each other, so the midpoint of one diagonal equals the midpoint of the other. We test the three possible pairings of opposite vertices to find the fourth vertex \((x,y)\) with \(x > 7\).

- If (5,3) and (7,4) are opposite, their midpoint is (6, 3.5). The other opposite pair is (6,8) and \((x,y)\). Midpoint of (6,8) and \((x,y)\) is \(((6+x)/2, (8+y)/2)\). Equating gives \(x = 6\), \(y = -1\) (not \(x > 7\)).
- If (5,3) and (6,8) are opposite, midpoint is (5.5, 5.5). The other pair is (7,4) and \((x,y)\). Equating gives \(x = 4\), \(y = 7\) (not \(x > 7\)).
- If (6,8) and (7,4) are opposite, midpoint is (6.5, 6). The other pair is (5,3) and \((x,y)\). Equating gives \(x = 8\), \(y = 9\) (\(x > 7\) satisfied).

Thus \(x = 8\), \(y = 9\), and \(x + y = 17\).

Answer: 17
